options: ensure that the legislature controls the judiciary
prevent the concentration of governmental powers in one authority
make the executive subordinate to political parties
questions.explanation: Separation of powers distributes governmental functions among different organs to prevent abuse and excessive concentration of power.

questions.text: When the legislature refuses to approve an executive expenditure, it is exercising its
questions.explanation: Control over public expenditure is an important means by which the legislature checks the executive.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the concept of constitutional supremacy
options: The executive is superior to the constitution
All institutions and laws are subject to the constitution
questions.explanation: Constitutional supremacy means the constitution is the highest legal authority and government institutions must operate within it.

questions.text: A constitution that can be amended by the same procedure used for ordinary legislation is
questions.explanation: A flexible constitution can be amended relatively easily through the ordinary legislative process.

questions.text: The strongest argument for an independent judiciary is that it
options: allows judges to make political decisions
protects the judiciary from interference when interpreting and applying the law
makes courts superior to the constitution
questions.explanation: Judicial independence allows judges to make decisions impartially and without political pressure.

questions.text: A government is considered democratic when
options: political power is exercised without accountability
citizens participate in choosing those who govern them
questions.explanation: Democracy is based on popular participation, political choice, accountability and lawful government.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to undermine democratic government
questions.explanation: Suppressing opposition prevents genuine political competition and accountability.

questions.text: A major advantage of a two-party system is that it
options: tends to produce clear alternatives for voters
questions.explanation: Voters are often presented with clear competing alternatives, and governments may be more stable.

questions.text: One major disadvantage of a multi-party system is that it may
options: make coalition formation necessary and potentially produce unstable governments

options: extensive consultation with Nigerians in its development
questions.explanation: The constitution emerged from a process involving considerable consultation at different levels.

questions.text: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 was a turning point because it
questions.explanation: The 1954 constitution formally established federalism, giving regions substantial constitutional responsibilities.

questions.text: Indirect rule was more successful in Northern Nigeria primarily because
options: the emirate system provided centralized traditional authorities
questions.explanation: The British could govern more easily through the existing centralized emirate institutions.

questions.text: A major difficulty of indirect rule in many parts of Eastern Nigeria was the
options: absence of centralized traditional political structures in many communities
existence of a powerful emirate system
questions.explanation: Many Eastern communities had decentralized political systems, making the British model of indirect rule difficult to apply.

questions.text: Nigeria's transition to a republic in 1963 meant that
options: the British monarch ceased to be Nigeria's head of state
the parliamentary system was immediately abolished
questions.explanation: The 1963 Constitution made Nigeria a republic, replacing the British monarch as head of state with a Nigerian president.

questions.text: The 1979 Nigerian Constitution is significant because it
options: introduced the presidential system of government
questions.explanation: Nigeria's Second Republic operated under a presidential constitutional system.

questions.text: The primary responsibility of the UN Security Council is
options: maintenance of international peace and security
questions.explanation: The Security Council has primary UN responsibility for international peace and security.

questions.text: A major limitation of collective security under the United Nations is that
options: disagreement among powerful states can prevent effective collective action
the UN has no member states
questions.explanation: Political disagreements, particularly among the permanent members of the Security Council, can prevent decisive collective action.

questions.text: A constitution provides for the removal of a president only after a specified legislative procedure. This provision is primarily intended to
options: make the president immune from prosecution
prevent arbitrary removal of the executive
abolish legislative control over the executive
make the judiciary subordinate to the executive
questions.explanation: Constitutional removal procedures provide due process and stability, preventing arbitrary political removal.

questions.text: If a law passed by parliament conflicts with the constitution, the law can be declared invalid because of the principle of
questions.explanation: Where the constitution is supreme, ordinary legislation must conform to constitutional provisions.

questions.text: The effectiveness of separation of powers depends largely on
options: complete isolation of the organs of government
an effective system of checks and balances
questions.explanation: The organs must be separate in function while still being able to check one another lawfully.

questions.text: Which situation best illustrates abuse of executive power
options: A president implementing a law passed by parliament
An executive authority detaining political opponents without lawful justification
A minister answering questions in parliament
A court reviewing an executive decision
questions.explanation: Arbitrary detention of opponents is an example of unlawful use of governmental authority.

questions.text: The main purpose of fundamental human rights provisions in a constitution is to
options: protect individuals against unlawful interference by the state and others, subject to lawful limitations
prevent citizens from participating in politics
questions.explanation: Constitutional rights provide legal protection for individual freedoms, although many rights can be subject to lawful limitations.

questions.text: A government that repeatedly ignores court judgments is most directly undermining
questions.explanation: Respect for lawful judicial decisions is an important part of the rule of law.

questions.text: Judicial review is most important because it enables the courts to
options: examine whether government actions comply with the law or constitution
questions.explanation: Judicial review provides a mechanism for checking whether government actions are legally and constitutionally valid.

questions.text: In a parliamentary government, the resignation of a minister following a major disagreement with cabinet policy illustrates
questions.explanation: Ministers are expected to support collective cabinet decisions; serious disagreement may require resignation.

questions.text: Which of the following is most characteristic of a parliamentary system
options: The executive is completely independent of the legislature
The government depends on legislative confidence
The president is always directly elected
Ministers cannot be members of parliament
questions.explanation: A parliamentary government survives only while it maintains the confidence of the legislature.

questions.text: A major advantage of a presidential system is that
options: the fixed constitutional tenure can provide executive stability
the executive is controlled entirely by parliament
questions.explanation: Presidential systems generally provide a fixed term, subject to constitutional removal procedures.

questions.text: A legislature with two chambers is described as
questions.explanation: Bicameralism means a legislature consists of two chambers.

questions.text: One major argument for a second legislative chamber is that it
options: can provide additional scrutiny of bills
questions.explanation: A second chamber can act as an additional reviewing and scrutinizing body.

questions.text: A party that wins 51% of votes but receives almost all legislative seats illustrates a weakness associated with
questions.explanation: Majoritarian systems can produce disproportionate seat distributions compared with vote shares.

questions.text: Which electoral arrangement is most likely to give minority parties legislative representation proportional to their support
questions.explanation: Proportional representation is designed to translate votes into seats more proportionately.

questions.text: The main purpose of voter registration is to
options: determine which political party will win
establish the eligibility and identity of persons entitled to vote
questions.explanation: Voter registration establishes the electoral roll and helps ensure that eligible persons can vote.

questions.text: If a voter is threatened with losing employment unless they vote for a particular candidate, the principle most directly violated is
options: secrecy and freedom of choice in voting
questions.explanation: Voters should be able to make their electoral choices freely and without coercion.

questions.text: A political party is more likely to survive beyond a single election when it
options: develops strong organization and a broad support base
has no clear ideology or programme
questions.explanation: Strong organization, membership and a broad support base promote party institutionalization and continuity.

questions.text: A pressure group that represents doctors is most likely to influence government by
options: providing expert information on health policy
questions.explanation: Specialized groups can influence policymakers through expertise, lobbying and policy advocacy.

questions.text: Political participation includes
options: activities through which citizens attempt to influence government and public affairs
questions.explanation: Participation includes voting, campaigning, contacting officials, demonstrations, party activity and other lawful political activities.

questions.text: A citizen who believes that their political actions can influence government decisions has a high level of
questions.explanation: Political efficacy is the belief that one's participation can make a difference in politics.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an essential element of a state
questions.explanation: A state requires population, territory, government and sovereignty. Political parties are not essential elements.

questions.text: The ability of a state to make decisions without being legally subordinate to another state demonstrates
questions.explanation: External sovereignty refers to independence from external political authority.

questions.text: The concept of legitimacy is important because a government with legitimacy
options: is generally regarded as having a rightful claim to exercise authority
questions.explanation: Legitimacy concerns the accepted rightfulness of political authority, not unlimited power.

questions.text: According to John Locke, government loses legitimacy when it
options: violates the natural rights for which government exists
questions.explanation: Locke argued that government exists to protect rights; serious violation can undermine its legitimacy and the people's obligation to obey.

questions.text: A major difference between a federation and a unitary state is that in a federation
options: component governments possess constitutionally protected powers
questions.explanation: Federal component units have powers that are constitutionally recognized, unlike ordinary local authorities in a unitary system.

questions.text: If the central government can abolish local governments whenever it wishes, the system is more likely to be
questions.explanation: In a unitary system, subnational authorities generally derive their powers from the central constitutional/legal authority.

questions.text: One major problem of federalism in a developing country may be
options: duplication of functions and high administrative costs
lack of constitutional division of powers
questions.explanation: Multiple governmental levels may create overlapping responsibilities and increased expenditure.

questions.text: Revenue allocation becomes particularly contentious in a federation when
options: different regions contribute different amounts to national revenue
questions.explanation: Differences in resource contribution and development needs often create disagreements over how revenue should be shared.

questions.text: The principle of derivation gives particular consideration to
options: the number of judges in each state
questions.explanation: Derivation allocates a share of revenue based on the source or origin of the revenue.

questions.text: The primary advantage of local government is that it
options: brings government closer to the people
questions.explanation: Local government promotes grassroots participation and delivery of local services.

questions.text: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 is historically significant because it
options: introduced the elective principle on a limited basis
questions.explanation: It introduced limited elective representation in Lagos and Calabar.

questions.text: The Richards Constitution of 1946 attempted to
options: promote regional representation within the colonial system
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution emphasized regional structures and representation.

questions.text: Which feature most distinguishes the Macpherson Constitution from the Richards Constitution
options: Greater Nigerian participation in its preparation
questions.explanation: The Macpherson Constitution followed a process involving extensive consultation with Nigerians.

questions.text: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 is important because it
questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution formally established the federal structure.

questions.text: Indirect rule was relatively successful in Northern Nigeria because
options: centralized traditional institutions could be used by the colonial administration
there were no established political structures
colonial administrators avoided using local rulers
questions.explanation: Existing emirate institutions made it easier for Britain to govern through traditional authorities.

questions.text: The failure of the warrant chief system in parts of Eastern Nigeria was largely due to
options: the decentralized nature of many indigenous political systems
questions.explanation: The British attempted to impose centralized authority where many communities traditionally had decentralized systems, causing resistance.

questions.text: Nigeria became a republic in 1963 primarily because
options: the British monarch ceased to be the country's constitutional head of state
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a republic while retaining a parliamentary system, with a Nigerian president replacing the British monarch as head of state.

questions.text: The introduction of presidential government in Nigeria in 1979 was significant because it
options: strengthened the separation between the executive and legislature
questions.explanation: The presidential system introduced a clearer institutional separation of executive and legislative powers.

questions.text: The primary reason for establishing the African Union was to
options: promote greater African cooperation, integration and collective action
questions.explanation: The AU promotes African unity, integration, peace, security and development.

questions.text: The principle of non-intervention in international relations is based mainly on respect for
questions.explanation: Sovereign states generally have authority over their internal affairs, so other states should not unlawfully interfere in those matters.

topic_questions.text: A political system is more likely to remain stable when citizens accept its institutions as legitimate, even when they disagree with particular government policies. This situation best illustrates the importance of
topic_questions.explanation: Political legitimacy exists when citizens recognize and accept the authority of political institutions and leaders.

topic_questions.text: In a society where citizens acquire political attitudes mainly through family discussions, school activities, religious organizations and the mass media, the process involved is best described as
topic_questions.explanation: Political socialization is the process through which individuals acquire political values, attitudes and orientations.

topic_questions.text: A newly elected government introduces policies that are unpopular but constitutionally authorized. If citizens continue to obey the government because they recognize its lawful authority, the situation demonstrates
topic_questions.explanation: Political obligation refers to the willingness of citizens to recognize and comply with legitimate political authority.

topic_questions.text: When citizens deliberately avoid elections, political meetings and other lawful political activities because they believe their participation cannot influence government decisions, the behaviour is known as
topic_questions.explanation: Political apathy is a lack of interest or willingness to participate in political activities.

topic_questions.text: A political party organizes rallies, distributes campaign materials and encourages supporters to vote for its candidates. The primary political process being promoted is
topic_questions.explanation: Political mobilization involves encouraging and organizing citizens to participate in political activities.

topic_questions.text: In a community, young people who initially show little interest in public affairs become politically active after participating in student union elections and civic education programmes. This change is mainly an outcome of
topic_questions.explanation: Political socialization can develop political awareness and participation through institutions such as schools and associations.

topic_questions.text: A government that derives its authority from established constitutional procedures is fundamentally different from one that maintains power primarily through force because the former possesses greater
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutional authority generally provides legitimacy because power is exercised according to accepted legal procedures.

topic_questions.text: The tendency of individuals to develop political beliefs that resemble those of their parents, especially during childhood, demonstrates the influence of the
topic_questions.explanation: The family is usually one of the earliest and most influential agents of political socialization.

topic_questions.text: A citizen who writes petitions to government officials, attends peaceful political demonstrations and participates in public consultations is engaging primarily in
topic_questions.explanation: Political participation includes lawful activities through which citizens seek to influence public decisions.

topic_questions.text: Political participation is considered more meaningful in a democracy when citizens are able to
options: influence public affairs through lawful political activities
avoid all contact with political institutions
accept every government decision without criticism
allow only political elites to make public decisions
topic_questions.explanation: Meaningful participation allows citizens to influence political decisions through lawful means.

topic_questions.text: A political party selects some of its active members to contest legislative seats after assessing their leadership abilities and commitment to party policies. This activity is an example of
topic_questions.explanation: Political recruitment involves identifying and preparing individuals for political leadership or public office.

topic_questions.text: When citizens become increasingly detached from political institutions because they feel that government does not respond to their interests, the resulting condition is best described as
topic_questions.explanation: Political alienation occurs when individuals feel separated from or powerless within the political system.

topic_questions.text: Which situation most clearly demonstrates the role of the mass media as an agent of political socialization?
options: A newspaper explains the functions of government institutions to its readers
A court sentences a person for violating electoral laws
A parliament approves the national budget
A political party registers new candidates
topic_questions.explanation: The mass media contributes to political socialization by transmitting political information and values to citizens.

topic_questions.text: A government introduces civic education in secondary schools to teach students about constitutional rights, political institutions and responsible citizenship. The immediate political objective is to promote
topic_questions.explanation: Civic education helps individuals acquire political knowledge, values and attitudes, making it an important form of political socialization.

topic_questions.text: If voters support a candidate because they believe the candidate will protect their community's interests, their behaviour demonstrates that political participation may be influenced by
topic_questions.explanation: Political attitudes, interests and perceptions commonly influence how citizens participate in political activities.

topic_questions.text: A political culture in which citizens generally trust public institutions, obey lawful decisions and regard political participation as valuable is most likely to encourage
topic_questions.explanation: A supportive political culture can strengthen legitimacy, participation and stability in a democratic system.

topic_questions.text: The belief held by citizens about the appropriate role of government and the expected behaviour of political leaders forms part of a society's
topic_questions.explanation: Political culture consists of citizens' shared attitudes, beliefs and values concerning politics and government.

topic_questions.text: In a political system, citizens who regularly vote, attend party meetings and communicate with elected representatives are displaying a relatively high level of
topic_questions.explanation: Voting, attending political meetings and contacting representatives are recognized forms of political participation.

topic_questions.text: A citizen disagrees with a government policy but obeys the law while using petitions, public debate and lawful protest to seek a change. This behaviour best reflects
topic_questions.explanation: Responsible political participation allows citizens to challenge policies through lawful and peaceful methods.

topic_questions.text: The ability of a political system to secure compliance with decisions while maintaining citizens' acceptance of its authority is closely associated with
topic_questions.explanation: Legitimacy strengthens a government's ability to obtain voluntary acceptance of its authority.

topic_questions.text: A political party deliberately spreads false information about an opposing party in order to influence voters. This action is most accurately regarded as
topic_questions.explanation: Propaganda involves deliberately presenting information, often selectively or misleadingly, to influence political attitudes or behaviour.

topic_questions.text: Which development is most likely to reduce political apathy among young citizens?
options: Increasing opportunities for meaningful civic participation
Limiting citizens' access to public officials
topic_questions.explanation: Meaningful opportunities for civic participation can increase political interest and encourage active citizenship.

topic_questions.text: When political values acquired during childhood remain influential in determining a person's later political choices, this illustrates that political socialization is often
topic_questions.explanation: Political socialization begins early but can continue throughout an individual's life as experiences and environments change.

topic_questions.text: A political system where citizens believe that government decisions can be influenced through elections, petitions and public debate is likely to have a political culture characterized by
topic_questions.explanation: A participant political culture is characterized by citizens' awareness of and involvement in political processes.

topic_questions.text: In a society where most citizens know little about national politics and rarely expect government to affect their lives, the dominant political orientation is closest to
topic_questions.explanation: Parochial political culture involves limited awareness or interest in national political institutions and processes.

topic_questions.text: Citizens who recognize government authority but mainly regard themselves as recipients of government decisions rather than active participants demonstrate a
topic_questions.explanation: In a subject orientation, citizens are aware of government authority but have limited involvement in influencing political decisions.

topic_questions.text: A government that consistently violates constitutional procedures may gradually lose citizens' willingness to accept its authority. The most direct political consequence is a decline in
topic_questions.explanation: Persistent violations of constitutional procedures can weaken citizens' belief that government authority is legitimate.

topic_questions.text: A student who becomes politically active after repeatedly discussing public issues with teachers and classmates is experiencing political socialization through
topic_questions.explanation: Schools and peer groups are important agents through which individuals develop political knowledge and attitudes.

topic_questions.text: The process through which political parties, government agencies and civil society organizations encourage citizens to support particular political objectives is best described as
topic_questions.explanation: Political mobilization involves organizing and encouraging people to participate in pursuit of political objectives.

topic_questions.text: A citizen refuses to vote because every candidate is perceived as equally incapable of addressing public problems. This behaviour most directly represents
topic_questions.explanation: Refusing to participate because of a lack of political interest or confidence is a common manifestation of political apathy.

topic_questions.text: Where political parties compete freely, citizens have access to political information and peaceful changes of government occur through elections, the political system demonstrates a high degree of
topic_questions.explanation: Competitive elections, political information and peaceful transfers of power are central features of democratic participation.

topic_questions.text: A political leader who repeatedly consults citizens, responds to public criticism and explains government decisions is most likely strengthening
topic_questions.explanation: Responsiveness and accountability can strengthen citizens' confidence in the legitimacy of political authority.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes political participation from political socialization?
options: Participation concerns political action, while socialization concerns the acquisition of political orientations
Participation occurs only in democratic states, while socialization occurs only in traditional societies
Participation is compulsory, while socialization is always voluntary
Participation concerns government officials, while socialization concerns only voters
topic_questions.explanation: Political participation involves political actions, while political socialization is the process through which political values and orientations are acquired.

topic_questions.text: A government-controlled media organization broadcasts only favourable information about government performance and suppresses serious criticism. The principal political purpose of such communication is
topic_questions.explanation: Selective communication designed to influence public attitudes in favour of government is political propaganda.

topic_questions.text: When citizens believe that political institutions are responsive to their demands and that their participation can produce meaningful outcomes, they are more likely to develop
topic_questions.explanation: Political efficacy is the belief that individuals can understand politics and influence political outcomes.

topic_questions.text: A person may have a strong interest in politics but rarely participate because of fear of discrimination or retaliation. This situation demonstrates that political participation can be restricted by
topic_questions.explanation: Fear, intimidation and threats can discourage citizens from participating freely in political activities.

topic_questions.text: A community leader teaches young residents that political disagreements should be resolved through dialogue, elections and lawful procedures. This teaching primarily contributes to the development of
topic_questions.explanation: Teaching peaceful and lawful methods of political engagement promotes democratic political values.

topic_questions.text: A political party uses internal elections, debates and leadership training to prepare members for future public office. The activity combines political recruitment with
topic_questions.explanation: Leadership training and internal political activities help members acquire political values and skills while preparing them for leadership.

topic_questions.text: If citizens participate in politics only during elections but remain largely inactive between elections, their pattern of participation can best be described as
topic_questions.explanation: Participation restricted mainly to voting represents a relatively limited form of political participation.

topic_questions.text: A government establishes public forums where citizens can question ministers and comment on proposed policies before decisions are made. This measure is most likely to increase
topic_questions.explanation: Public consultation creates opportunities for citizens to participate in policy-making and express their views.

topic_questions.text: When a political party deliberately selects candidates from different ethnic, regional and social backgrounds to broaden its appeal, the strategy is primarily intended to promote
topic_questions.explanation: Political integration involves bringing diverse groups into a common political framework and strengthening their sense of shared participation.

topic_questions.text: The repeated use of family discussions, community meetings, school programmes and media campaigns to transmit similar political values is most likely to produce
topic_questions.explanation: Multiple agents transmitting political values contribute to the process of political socialization.

topic_questions.text: A citizen believes that voting is important, follows political news and regularly contacts representatives about public problems. This behaviour indicates both political awareness and
topic_questions.explanation: The citizen combines political awareness with active participation in political processes.

topic_questions.text: A society in which citizens are encouraged to question public officials, demand explanations for government decisions and monitor public spending is promoting
topic_questions.explanation: Political accountability requires public officials to explain and justify their actions to citizens and institutions.

topic_questions.text: A citizen's political opinions change after exposure to new information, economic experiences and interactions with different social groups. This demonstrates that political attitudes are
options: capable of changing through social experience
topic_questions.explanation: Political attitudes can change as individuals encounter new information, experiences and social influences.

topic_questions.text: A government bans peaceful political meetings and arrests individuals for expressing lawful opposition. Such measures are most likely to produce
topic_questions.explanation: Political repression involves restricting political freedoms or suppressing opposition through coercive measures.

topic_questions.text: When citizens participate in elections because they believe doing so gives them an opportunity to influence who governs them, their behaviour reflects
topic_questions.explanation: Political efficacy is reflected in the belief that one's political actions can influence government and political outcomes.

topic_questions.text: A political culture that encourages compromise, tolerance of opposing views and acceptance of lawful electoral outcomes is particularly important for
topic_questions.explanation: Tolerance, compromise and acceptance of legitimate outcomes help democratic institutions function peacefully and remain stable.

topic_questions.text: A political party establishes youth wings, organizes leadership seminars and encourages young members to contest internal elections. The party is primarily seeking to
topic_questions.explanation: Youth wings and leadership development programmes can identify and prepare future political leaders.

topic_questions.text: When citizens deliberately spread accurate information about voting procedures and encourage others to participate peacefully in elections, they are contributing to
topic_questions.explanation: Encouraging citizens to participate in elections is a form of political mobilization.

topic_questions.text: The long-term transmission of political beliefs from parents to children can strengthen continuity in a political system, but it may also
options: reproduce existing political attitudes across generations
eliminate the influence of schools and media
topic_questions.explanation: Family-based socialization can reproduce political values across generations, although other agents may also influence individuals.

topic_questions.text: A citizen who is politically informed but chooses not to participate because of repeated disappointment with political leaders is exhibiting a combination of political awareness and
topic_questions.explanation: A politically informed person may still become apathetic when disappointment reduces willingness to participate.

topic_questions.text: A political system is more likely to enjoy broad legitimacy when citizens perceive that political authority is exercised
options: according to accepted legal and political rules
topic_questions.explanation: Citizens are more likely to regard authority as legitimate when it operates according to accepted laws and political rules.

topic_questions.text: A national civic programme teaches citizens how to evaluate political claims, distinguish reliable information from misinformation and engage respectfully with opposing views. Its strongest contribution is to
topic_questions.explanation: Civic education that develops critical political understanding can promote informed and responsible participation.

topic_questions.text: Where citizens regard political opponents as legitimate competitors rather than enemies and accept that power may change hands through elections, the political culture supports
topic_questions.explanation: Recognizing opponents and accepting peaceful transfers of power are important elements of democratic political competition.

topic_questions.text: A political community possesses a defined territory, a permanent population, an organized government and the authority to make and enforce laws without being legally subordinate to another state. Which essential characteristic is most clearly established by this description?
topic_questions.explanation: Sovereignty refers to the supreme and independent authority of a state within its territory.

topic_questions.text: Two groups may occupy the same territory and possess common citizenship while maintaining different historical identities and cultural traditions. This situation demonstrates that a nation is primarily distinguished from a state by its
options: shared sense of identity and common consciousness
topic_questions.explanation: A nation is based largely on shared identity, history, culture or consciousness, whereas a state has legal and territorial characteristics.

topic_questions.text: A government may change after an election while the territory, population and international identity of the country remain substantially the same. This indicates that government differs from the state because government is
options: the permanent legal identity of a country
the machinery through which the state is administered
the supreme authority of the state
topic_questions.explanation: Government refers to the institutions and officials through which the state exercises its authority.

topic_questions.text: A territory has a permanent population and a recognized government, but its leaders cannot independently determine foreign or domestic policies because another country exercises ultimate authority over it. The territory lacks
topic_questions.explanation: A state must possess sovereignty, meaning supreme and independent authority over its affairs.

topic_questions.text: When a constitution declares that no public authority may exercise powers beyond those granted by law, the provision primarily seeks to prevent
topic_questions.explanation: Limiting official powers through law prevents arbitrary government and promotes constitutionalism.

topic_questions.text: A state may retain its legal personality and territorial identity even when the individuals occupying public offices change after an election. This permanence is mainly associated with the
topic_questions.explanation: The state is a continuing political entity, whereas governments and office holders may change.

topic_questions.text: A constitution is described as supreme when
options: all political parties agree with every provision in it
its provisions have authority over ordinary laws and governmental actions
only the executive can interpret its provisions
it cannot be amended under any circumstances
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutional supremacy means ordinary laws and governmental actions must conform to the constitution.

topic_questions.text: In a state where ultimate political authority is constitutionally derived from the people and exercised through elected representatives, the principle involved is
topic_questions.explanation: Popular sovereignty means that ultimate political authority is vested in the people.

topic_questions.text: A country has a common language, historical experience and strong cultural identity, but its people are divided among several sovereign states. The situation shows that
options: every nation must constitute one sovereign state
a state can exist without any population
a nation and a state are always identical
a nation may exist without forming a single sovereign state
topic_questions.explanation: A nation is based on shared identity and consciousness and may exist across the boundaries of more than one state.

topic_questions.text: Which situation most clearly demonstrates the internal aspect of state sovereignty?
options: A state negotiates a treaty with another country
A state maintains an embassy abroad
A state exercises supreme authority over persons and institutions within its territory
A state joins an international organization
topic_questions.explanation: Internal sovereignty concerns the state's supreme authority over individuals and institutions within its territory.

topic_questions.text: A state refuses to accept instructions from another sovereign state concerning how it should organize its domestic administration. This illustrates
topic_questions.explanation: External sovereignty refers to independence from external control or interference by other states.

topic_questions.text: A written constitution contains provisions that require a special procedure involving approval by a specified proportion of legislators and, in some cases, the states before amendment. Such a constitution is best described as
topic_questions.explanation: A rigid constitution requires a special and more difficult procedure for amendment than ordinary legislation.

topic_questions.text: A constitution that can be amended through substantially the same legislative procedure used for ordinary laws is classified as
topic_questions.explanation: A flexible constitution can generally be amended through the ordinary law-making process.

topic_questions.text: A constitution contains detailed provisions defining governmental institutions, citizens' rights and procedures for exercising public power. Its principal function is to
options: provide a framework for the organization and limitation of government
guarantee that no government can ever change
transfer sovereignty permanently to the legislature
topic_questions.explanation: A constitution establishes governmental structures, defines powers and often protects citizens against governmental abuse.

topic_questions.text: The authority of a state is considered legitimate rather than merely coercive when citizens generally accept the right of its institutions to make binding decisions. This acceptance is known as
topic_questions.explanation: Legitimacy is the belief that political authority is rightful and should be obeyed.

topic_questions.text: A government introduces a new law that conflicts directly with a provision of the constitution. In a system operating under constitutional supremacy, the conflicting law should
options: be treated as superior because it was recently enacted
remain valid whenever the executive supports it
be invalid to the extent that it conflicts with the constitution
topic_questions.explanation: Under constitutional supremacy, ordinary legislation must conform to the constitution.

topic_questions.text: A political entity possesses a government and population but has no clearly defined territorial boundaries. Which essential element of statehood is most obviously absent?
topic_questions.explanation: A defined territory is one of the essential characteristics of a state.

topic_questions.text: The distinction between a state and a government is most clearly demonstrated by the fact that
options: a government has no relationship with the state
governments may change while the state continues to exist
the state exists only when an election is held
a state consists only of elected officials
topic_questions.explanation: Governments are temporary administrations, while the state is the continuing political entity.

topic_questions.text: A group of people develops a strong sense of belonging based on common ancestry, language and historical experiences but does not possess a sovereign territory of its own. It is more accurately described as a
topic_questions.explanation: A nation may be formed by people sharing common identity and historical consciousness without possessing an independent state.

topic_questions.text: When a constitution distributes governmental powers among different institutions so that no single institution can exercise unlimited authority, it primarily seeks to
topic_questions.explanation: Distributing and limiting powers helps prevent concentration and abuse of political authority.

topic_questions.text: A constitution may be regarded as a source of political stability because it
options: provides agreed rules for the exercise and transfer of political power
ensures that one political party remains permanently in office
prevents citizens from challenging government policies
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutions establish predictable rules governing political authority, institutions and changes of government.

topic_questions.text: A state with a single national government exercising ultimate authority over local administrative units is most consistent with a
topic_questions.explanation: In a unitary system, ultimate governmental authority is concentrated in the central government.

topic_questions.text: Where constituent units possess constitutionally guaranteed powers that cannot ordinarily be withdrawn by the central government acting alone, the arrangement is characteristic of
topic_questions.explanation: Federalism constitutionally divides powers between central and constituent governments.

topic_questions.text: A constitution is described as federal when it
options: creates only one level of government
places all legislative authority in local governments
divides governmental powers constitutionally between central and constituent units
allows the executive to suspend all state institutions
topic_questions.explanation: A federal constitution allocates governmental powers between the central authority and constituent units.

topic_questions.text: A constitution that consists of customs, conventions, judicial decisions and statutes rather than being contained in one single document is commonly described as
topic_questions.explanation: An unwritten constitution derives from several sources rather than one comprehensive constitutional document.

topic_questions.text: The existence of a constitution alone does not guarantee constitutional government because constitutional government requires that
options: public authorities actually observe constitutional limitations
political parties be prohibited from opposing government
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutional government depends on the actual observance of constitutional rules and limitations.

topic_questions.text: A state enters into a treaty that limits how it may exercise certain powers in an agreed international area. The existence of such a treaty does not necessarily destroy sovereignty because
options: sovereignty requires absolute freedom from every agreement
states may voluntarily accept international obligations while retaining legal sovereignty
treaties automatically transfer sovereignty to foreign governments
international obligations apply only to private citizens
topic_questions.explanation: Sovereign states can voluntarily undertake international obligations without necessarily losing their status as sovereign states.

permanent rule by the incumbent party

transfer legislative power to the judiciary

make every government institution subordinate to local councils
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutional allocation of functions between levels of government is a defining feature of federal arrangements.

make citizens subject only to customary law
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutions commonly define and protect fundamental rights and impose duties on public authorities to respect them.

gives one ethnic group exclusive political rights
prevents citizens from participating in government
removes all regional interests from public life
topic_questions.explanation: Common constitutional institutions and rules can help unite diverse groups within a political community.

topic_questions.explanation: Government acts through public institutions to exercise and administer the authority of the state.

topic_questions.explanation: Constitutional supremacy places the constitution above ordinary governmental authority and laws.

topic_questions.text: A people may possess a strong national identity while being governed by different states because
options: national identity necessarily depends on one government
nationhood is based primarily on shared identity rather than the possession of sovereign government
topic_questions.explanation: Nationhood is primarily associated with shared identity and consciousness, which can exist across state boundaries.

its provisions are ignored during political crises
the executive can suspend all its limitations indefinitely
political parties determine its meaning without legal procedures
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutional limits are meaningful only when institutions enforce and public authorities respect them.

options: states can cooperate internationally without automatically ceasing to be sovereign
membership of an organization makes a state a province
topic_questions.explanation: States can cooperate and accept obligations through international organizations while retaining their sovereign status.

topic_questions.text: A constitution that is difficult to amend may protect political stability, but it can become problematic when
options: necessary institutional changes are prevented by excessive procedural difficulty
government institutions operate within legal limits
topic_questions.explanation: An excessively rigid constitution may hinder necessary reforms by making legitimate constitutional change too difficult.

topic_questions.text: The concept of sovereignty is most clearly demonstrated when a state
options: allows another state to appoint its ministers
permits foreign authorities to make its domestic laws
exercises supreme authority within its territory and independence externally
allows political parties to determine international treaties
topic_questions.explanation: Sovereignty combines supreme internal authority with independence from external control.

topic_questions.text: Where constitutional rules are regularly altered by ordinary legislation without any special procedure, the constitution is likely to be

topic_questions.text: A state whose government derives its authority from a constitution that clearly defines the powers of public institutions is practicing

topic_questions.explanation: A sovereign authority operating over a defined territory is fundamental to statehood, while nationhood centers on shared identity.

topic_questions.explanation: Popular sovereignty means that ultimate political authority rests with the people.

topic_questions.explanation: Political pluralism permits different political interests and groups to compete and express their views.

topic_questions.text: A public official is prosecuted for an offence committed while in office and cannot prevent the case merely by relying on official position. This situation best demonstrates
topic_questions.explanation: Equality before the law requires public officials and ordinary citizens to be subject to the law.

topic_questions.text: A constitution guarantees citizens freedom of expression but permits restrictions that are prescribed by law and necessary to protect public safety. This illustrates that fundamental rights

topic_questions.explanation: Many rights are protected but may be lawfully limited under constitutionally recognized circumstances.

topic_questions.text: A government arrests an opposition leader without trial and refuses to disclose the legal basis for the detention. The principle most directly threatened by this action is
topic_questions.explanation: Due process requires government to follow established legal procedures before depriving a person of liberty.

topic_questions.text: The rule of law is most effectively strengthened when
options: government officials are exempt from legal accountability
laws are applied selectively according to political status
courts operate independently and laws apply equally
the executive determines which court decisions are valid
topic_questions.explanation: An independent judiciary and equality before the law are central requirements of the rule of law.

topic_questions.text: A democratic government is prevented from imprisoning a citizen merely for criticizing its policies because such protection is primarily associated with

topic_questions.text: A court declares a government regulation invalid because it violates a constitutionally protected right. The court is exercising its power of
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutional review enables courts to determine whether governmental actions comply with the constitution.

topic_questions.text: Which condition would most seriously weaken the rule of law in a democratic state?

topic_questions.text: A citizen who has attained the legal age and satisfies constitutional requirements is entitled to participate in choosing public officials. This is an exercise of the

topic_questions.text: A government introduces legislation that protects citizens from discrimination based on legally recognized grounds. Such legislation primarily promotes the principle of
topic_questions.explanation: Equality requires citizens to receive equal legal protection and prevents unjust discrimination.

topic_questions.text: A citizen accused of an offence is given adequate notice of the charge, access to legal representation and an opportunity to defend himself before an impartial court. These safeguards are elements of
topic_questions.explanation: Due process protects individuals by requiring fair and established legal procedures.

topic_questions.text: A legislature passes a law that retrospectively makes conduct criminal even though it was lawful when performed. Which principle is most directly violated?
topic_questions.explanation: The principle of legality generally requires that conduct should not be punished as criminal when it was not criminal under the law at the time.

topic_questions.text: The ability of citizens to challenge unlawful government action before an independent court is particularly important because it
options: makes the executive superior to the constitution
provides a legal remedy against abuse of public power
topic_questions.explanation: Judicial remedies allow citizens to seek protection when public authorities violate legal or constitutional rights.

topic_questions.text: A democratic government consults affected communities before adopting a major policy and allows citizens to submit objections. This practice primarily strengthens
topic_questions.explanation: Public consultation provides citizens with opportunities to participate in governmental decision-making.

topic_questions.text: A constitution protects a citizen's freedom to join a lawful association or political organization. This protection is most closely related to
topic_questions.explanation: Freedom of association protects the ability to form or join lawful groups and organizations.

topic_questions.text: The principle of majority rule in a democracy does not justify unlimited treatment of minorities because democratic government must also
options: allow the majority to suspend the constitution
topic_questions.explanation: Democracy combines majority decision-making with constitutional protection of fundamental rights, including minority rights.

topic_questions.text: A court refuses to hear a case because the plaintiff has not first used an available administrative remedy required by law. This reflects the importance of
topic_questions.explanation: Legal systems often require parties to follow prescribed procedures before judicial intervention.

topic_questions.text: A government allows journalists to investigate public expenditure and publish findings without prior political approval. The policy most directly supports
topic_questions.explanation: Freedom of the press enables journalists to investigate and communicate information about public affairs.

topic_questions.text: A person who becomes a citizen through naturalization may be required to satisfy statutory conditions before acquiring full citizenship rights. This indicates that citizenship can be acquired through
topic_questions.explanation: Naturalization is a legal process through which a non-citizen acquires citizenship after satisfying prescribed requirements.

topic_questions.text: A democratic constitution permits citizens to organize peaceful demonstrations but prohibits demonstrations that deliberately involve violence. This distinction recognizes the need to balance
topic_questions.explanation: Democratic freedoms may be regulated to protect public safety and order while preserving lawful political expression.

topic_questions.text: When a citizen loses the legal status of belonging to a country under circumstances provided by law, the situation concerns
topic_questions.explanation: Citizenship is the legal relationship between an individual and a state, including rights and obligations.

topic_questions.text: A government cannot lawfully punish a person for an act that was not prohibited by law at the time it was committed. This requirement is a safeguard against
topic_questions.explanation: The prohibition against retroactive criminal punishment protects citizens from being punished under laws created after their conduct.

topic_questions.text: A democratic state permits an unpopular religious group to practice its faith peacefully despite opposition from the majority. This best demonstrates
topic_questions.explanation: Religious tolerance protects lawful religious practice and respects diversity within society.

topic_questions.text: An individual is detained by security officials and denied access to a court for an indefinite period. Which democratic safeguard is most clearly threatened?

topic_questions.explanation: Access to justice allows individuals to challenge unlawful detention and seek judicial protection.

topic_questions.text: A constitution guarantees citizens the right to move freely within the country, subject to lawful restrictions. This is an example of
topic_questions.explanation: Freedom of movement protects the lawful ability of citizens to travel and reside within the state.

topic_questions.text: A government uses its security agencies to prevent an opposition party from holding a peaceful meeting without a lawful justification. Such conduct most directly threatens
topic_questions.explanation: Suppressing lawful political meetings restricts citizens' political freedoms and association.

topic_questions.text: The principle that governmental decisions must be based on established laws rather than personal preferences of officials is central to
topic_questions.explanation: The rule of law requires public authorities to act according to established legal rules.

topic_questions.text: A government introduces emergency measures during a serious crisis but subjects those measures to constitutional limits and judicial oversight. This demonstrates that even during emergencies
options: governmental power should remain subject to law
topic_questions.explanation: Emergency powers in a constitutional democracy remain subject to legal and constitutional constraints.

topic_questions.text: A citizen is prevented from standing for public office solely because of an arbitrary administrative decision, despite meeting all legal requirements. The decision most directly undermines
topic_questions.explanation: Unlawful exclusion from political opportunities can violate the principle of political equality.

topic_questions.text: A court orders the release of a person whose detention has no lawful basis. The decision illustrates the judiciary's role in
topic_questions.explanation: Courts protect individual liberty by providing remedies against unlawful detention.

topic_questions.text: A democratic system permits peaceful criticism of government because disagreement with public policy is not itself treated as a criminal offence. This is primarily an expression of
topic_questions.explanation: Freedom of expression protects lawful criticism and communication of political opinions.

topic_questions.text: A citizen who satisfies the legal requirements for citizenship is expected to obey the laws of the state and may also enjoy political rights. This relationship illustrates that citizenship involves

topic_questions.text: A government decides to restrict a public gathering because credible evidence indicates an immediate threat of violence, while providing a lawful avenue for challenging the restriction. The arrangement seeks to balance

topic_questions.text: An independent electoral body applies the same voting rules to supporters of the ruling party and opposition parties. This practice reinforces

topic_questions.text: A government publishes the reasons for restricting a citizen's liberty and provides an opportunity for the decision to be reviewed by a court. This most clearly supports
topic_questions.explanation: Due process requires fair procedures and opportunities to challenge governmental decisions affecting legal rights.

topic_questions.text: A person born outside a country acquires its nationality after meeting statutory conditions and completing a formal legal process. The process is best described as

topic_questions.explanation: Judicial challenge to unlawful government action reinforces legal accountability of public authorities.

topic_questions.explanation: Using administrative authority to punish lawful political criticism constitutes an abuse of public power.

options: become legally enforceable rather than merely declaratory
can be exercised only by public officials
cannot be limited under any circumstance
are dependent entirely on political parties
topic_questions.explanation: Judicial remedies make constitutional rights enforceable by allowing courts to provide protection when violations occur.

topic_questions.explanation: Respect for rights, opposition, judicial authority and constitutional limits are central features of constitutional democracy.

represent only the interests of professional associations
gain political power through constitutional means

topic_questions.explanation: Pressure groups can influence policy by supplying expertise and lobbying decision-makers.

protect voters from intimidation over their choices
allow electoral officers to choose winners

topic_questions.explanation: Public opinion refers to the views and attitudes held by members of society on public issues.

the number of campaign rallies held

elections must always produce coalition governments

topic_questions.explanation: Elections allow citizens to reward or punish political leaders based partly on their performance and commitments.

options: combines public support with lawful advocacy
prevents citizens from expressing alternative views
topic_questions.explanation: Lawful advocacy supported by public awareness can increase a pressure group's influence on policymakers.

options: loses because an absolute majority is required
wins because the candidate has the plurality
must be appointed by the judiciary

must always support the ruling party

options: allows participants to understand the rules governing the election
guarantees that the incumbent will win
removes the need for political parties

each organ performs constitutionally assigned functions

topic_questions.text: A major characteristic of a unitary system is that political authority is primarily

exercised by independent states joined for limited purposes
divided equally among autonomous regional governments
concentrated in a central government, which may delegate powers to lower authorities
topic_questions.explanation: In a unitary system, the central government possesses ultimate constitutional authority and may delegate powers to subordinate authorities.

topic_questions.text: The strongest constitutional distinction between a federation and a unitary state is that in a federation
options: local governments must be completely independent of the centre
the constitution distributes governmental powers between central and regional governments
the central government has unlimited power over all regions
regional governments may withdraw from the federation whenever they choose
topic_questions.explanation: Federal constitutions constitutionally allocate powers between the central authority and constituent units.

topic_questions.text: A country adopts a constitution in which the central government can alter the powers of provincial governments without their constitutional consent. This arrangement is most consistent with
topic_questions.explanation: In a unitary system, the central authority has ultimate constitutional control over subordinate governmental units.

topic_questions.text: One major weakness commonly associated with a highly centralized unitary system is that it may
options: reduce local participation in governmental decision-making
make the central government constitutionally weak
give constituent states excessive sovereign powers
prevent national policies from being implemented uniformly
topic_questions.explanation: Excessive centralization can weaken local initiative and reduce opportunities for grassroots participation.

topic_questions.text: The division of legislative powers into exclusive, concurrent and residual areas in a federation is primarily intended to
options: abolish the authority of regional governments
make the judiciary superior to the legislature
define the constitutional responsibilities of different levels of government
allow each level of government to exercise unlimited powers
topic_questions.explanation: Such divisions clarify which governmental level has authority over particular matters.

topic_questions.text: A federal arrangement is particularly suitable for a country with substantial regional diversity because it can
options: allow regional governments to address local interests while maintaining national unity
prevent the central government from making national policies
topic_questions.explanation: Federalism can accommodate diversity by granting constituent units authority over matters of local concern.

topic_questions.text: Which situation best illustrates a confederal arrangement?
options: A central government appoints all regional governors

Two levels of government derive authority directly from a constitution
Independent states cooperate through a common body while retaining substantial sovereignty
topic_questions.explanation: A confederation is an association of sovereign states that delegate limited functions to a common institution.

topic_questions.text: A major weakness of confederation as a form of government is that the common authority may

become too powerful over completely subordinate regions
abolish the sovereignty of all member states automatically
prevent member states from conducting foreign relations
topic_questions.explanation: Because member states retain substantial sovereignty, the central confederal authority may have weak enforcement powers.

topic_questions.text: In a presidential system, the president is normally
options: selected by the legislature from among its members
both head of state and head of government
required to resign immediately after losing a parliamentary vote
topic_questions.explanation: The president in a presidential system commonly combines the roles of head of state and head of government.

topic_questions.text: A government is described as parliamentary when the executive authority is generally
options: drawn from and politically accountable to the legislature
topic_questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the executive emerges from the legislature and depends on its confidence.

topic_questions.text: If a prime minister loses the confidence of the majority in parliament and cannot form another majority, the most likely constitutional consequence is
options: the judiciary automatically takes over government
the monarch or president assumes legislative powers
the government resigns or a new parliamentary government is formed
topic_questions.explanation: Loss of parliamentary confidence can require the government to resign or lead to the formation of another government.

topic_questions.text: A notable advantage of the parliamentary system is that it can facilitate
options: quick removal of an ineffective government through a loss of legislative confidence
complete separation between the executive and legislature
permanent tenure for the prime minister
topic_questions.explanation: Parliamentary governments can be replaced relatively quickly when they lose legislative confidence.

topic_questions.text: A principal feature that distinguishes a presidential system from a parliamentary system is that in the presidential system
options: the executive normally has a fixed constitutional tenure independent of legislative confidence
the legislature appoints the president as prime minister
the cabinet collectively controls the courts
topic_questions.explanation: Presidential executives generally serve fixed constitutional terms and do not depend on ordinary legislative confidence to remain in office.

topic_questions.text: One possible disadvantage of presidential government when the president and legislative majority belong to opposing parties is
options: fusion of the judiciary and legislature
institutional deadlock over legislation and policy
immediate replacement of the president by parliament
topic_questions.explanation: Separate electoral mandates can produce conflict between the executive and legislature, resulting in policy deadlock.

serve independently of the head of government
are expected to publicly support agreed government policy or resign

options: abolishing the office of prime minister
having both a president and a prime minister with constitutionally defined executive roles
making the legislature subordinate to the courts
giving all executive authority to local governments

remove the need for a national government
combine national political unity with a degree of regional autonomy

all governmental institutions must act within powers granted by the constitution
the central government may suspend the constitution permanently
political parties determine the meaning of constitutional provisions
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutional supremacy requires all governmental authorities to operate within the limits established by the constitution.

topic_questions.text: If constituent units in a federation have constitutionally protected powers that cannot be removed by ordinary central legislation, the arrangement demonstrates

options: the common authority normally derives stronger authority directly from citizens
member states have no independent political existence
regional units are subordinate to the national government

topic_questions.explanation: Confederal members remain substantially sovereign, whereas constituent units in a federation are not sovereign states.

the central government appoints every local official
regional governments are denied legislative authority
all political decisions are made in the capital
topic_questions.explanation: Federal arrangements can accommodate regional interests through participation at the centre and protected powers at the regional level.

a constitutionally prescribed procedure such as impeachment
a decision by the cabinet alone
automatic resignation after losing a party election

options: the executive is completely separate from parliament
regional governments appoint the national executive
the executive is drawn from the legislature
topic_questions.explanation: The parliamentary executive is normally formed from members of the legislature, particularly the governing majority.

options: central and constituent governments with constitutionally defined areas of authority
two competing presidents with equal constitutional powers
two separate sovereign countries under one monarch
a legislature and judiciary exercising identical powers
topic_questions.explanation: Federalism involves national and constituent governments whose powers are constitutionally allocated.

introduced elective representation into the Legislative Council

options: all Nigerians could vote directly for the governor
elective representation was restricted to a very small portion of the population
traditional rulers controlled the Legislative Council completely

options: gave greater recognition to regional representation
established Nigeria as an independent republic

the creation of the Nigerian republic

topic_questions.text: A major feature of Nigeria's 1963 Republican Constitution was the retention of
topic_questions.explanation: Although Nigeria became a republic, the parliamentary system was retained.

Nigeria operated a presidential system under military rule
the country was administered directly by Britain
topic_questions.explanation: The First Republic was the civilian parliamentary era following independence and preceding the first military coup.

topic_questions.text: The regional structure of the First Republic contributed to political competition because

all major parties operated only at the federal level
major political parties had strong regional bases and competing interests
topic_questions.explanation: Political parties had strong regional support bases, which intensified competition over federal power.
