the establishment of the Fourth Republic
the return to British colonial rule
the overthrow of the civilian government
topic_questions.explanation: The January 1966 coup ended the First Republic and brought military rule to Nigeria.

topic_questions.text: One constitutional consequence of military intervention in Nigeria was that
options: legislative institutions could be suspended while military decrees became important sources of law
political parties gained greater constitutional powers
topic_questions.explanation: Military governments commonly suspended or modified constitutional institutions and governed extensively through decrees.

topic_questions.text: The 1979 Constitution represented a major departure from the First Republic because it introduced
topic_questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution established a presidential system based partly on the United States model.

topic_questions.text: Under the 1979 presidential system, the President differed from the First Republic's Prime Minister because the President
options: was responsible to parliament through a vote of confidence
possessed a separate electoral mandate from the legislature
served as a ceremonial head of state only
topic_questions.explanation: The presidential system separated the executive's electoral mandate from that of the legislature.

topic_questions.text: The principle of federal character in Nigeria's constitutional development is primarily intended to
options: ensure that all political offices are filled by one region
give the federal government unlimited powers
promote broad representation and reduce domination by particular groups or regions
topic_questions.explanation: Federal character seeks to promote inclusiveness in national institutions and reduce perceived regional domination.

topic_questions.text: The 1979 Constitution introduced the presidential system partly because its framers sought to
options: reduce the weaknesses associated with the parliamentary model and strengthen separation of powers
make the legislature subordinate to traditional rulers
topic_questions.explanation: The presidential model was intended to strengthen separation of powers and avoid some problems associated with the earlier parliamentary system.

topic_questions.text: The Second Republic ended in 1983 when
options: the British government dissolved the federation
the military overthrew the civilian government
the Supreme Court suspended the constitution
topic_questions.explanation: A military coup in December 1983 ended the Second Republic.

topic_questions.text: The 1989 constitutional experiment is notable in Nigerian political history because it
options: was associated with a military-led transition toward a new political order
topic_questions.explanation: The 1989 Constitution formed part of the military government's attempt to establish a new civilian political order.

topic_questions.text: The Third Republic is generally associated with the period when Nigeria
options: attempted a return to civilian democratic government in the early 1990s
topic_questions.explanation: The Third Republic refers to the short-lived civilian democratic experiment of the early 1990s.

topic_questions.text: The annulment of the 12 June 1993 presidential election contributed significantly to
options: a major political crisis and interruption of the transition to civilian rule
the immediate establishment of the Fourth Republic
topic_questions.explanation: The annulment generated widespread political crisis and disrupted the transition programme.

topic_questions.text: The 1993 political crisis demonstrated the importance of
options: constitutional legitimacy and credible electoral processes
topic_questions.explanation: The crisis highlighted how disputed electoral legitimacy can undermine political stability.

topic_questions.text: The 1999 Constitution is associated with the beginning of Nigeria's
topic_questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution provided the constitutional basis for the Fourth Republic, which began in 1999.

topic_questions.text: A major similarity between Nigeria's 1979 and 1999 Constitutions is that both
options: made the monarch head of state
provided for a presidential federal system
topic_questions.explanation: Both constitutions established presidential government within a federal structure.

topic_questions.text: One major reason Nigeria's constitutional development has involved repeated changes is
options: the interaction of colonial legacies, regional interests, military interventions and attempts to manage diversity
the complete absence of political parties
the lack of any ethnic or regional differences
the permanent stability of civilian institutions
topic_questions.explanation: Nigeria's constitutional changes have reflected attempts to respond to political instability, diversity, regional interests and military intervention.

topic_questions.text: The creation of more states in Nigeria has generally been justified partly on the grounds that it can
options: bring government closer to the people and reduce perceived regional domination
topic_questions.explanation: State creation has often been justified as a way of improving representation, administration and political balance.

topic_questions.text: The 1963 Constitution's treatment of the regions differed from a unitary arrangement because the regions
options: were merely administrative departments of the federal government
topic_questions.explanation: The regions were constituent units with constitutionally recognized powers within the federation.

topic_questions.text: The constitutional principle that prevents the federal government from arbitrarily abolishing constitutionally recognized state powers is closely associated with
topic_questions.explanation: Federalism protects defined spheres of authority for constituent units through constitutional arrangements.

topic_questions.text: The colonial policy of indirect rule influenced Nigerian constitutional development by
options: strengthening the role of traditional authorities in local administration
topic_questions.explanation: Indirect rule relied substantially on traditional authorities as intermediaries in administering colonial territories.

topic_questions.text: One major political consequence of indirect rule in Nigeria was that it
options: created identical political institutions in every area
produced different administrative experiences across regions
abolished the authority of emirs and chiefs
made all Nigerians directly governed by elected representatives
topic_questions.explanation: Indirect rule operated differently across areas, contributing to variations in political and administrative development.

topic_questions.text: The amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria in 1914 is significant because it
options: brought the two colonial territories under a single administrative framework
topic_questions.explanation: The 1914 amalgamation united the Northern and Southern Protectorates under one colonial administration.

topic_questions.text: The constitutional development of Nigeria before independence was gradual partly because Britain
options: refused to establish any Nigerian political institutions
introduced reforms progressively while retaining ultimate colonial authority
topic_questions.explanation: Colonial constitutional reforms gradually expanded Nigerian participation while Britain retained ultimate authority until independence.

topic_questions.text: The elective principle under the Clifford Constitution was politically important because it
options: created an early institutional avenue for limited electoral participation
gave women and men equal voting rights throughout Nigeria
topic_questions.explanation: Although restricted, the elective principle introduced an important early form of electoral representation.

topic_questions.text: The Richards Constitution's emphasis on regional councils was partly intended to
options: replace all regional identities with one national identity
accommodate regional differences within the colonial constitutional structure
topic_questions.explanation: Regional institutions were used partly to recognize Nigeria's diverse political and social conditions.

topic_questions.text: A key lesson from the Macpherson Constitution was that constitutional reforms are more likely to gain legitimacy when they
options: involve meaningful participation by affected political communities
topic_questions.explanation: The Macpherson process demonstrated the importance of broad participation in constitutional development.

topic_questions.text: The federal arrangement established in 1954 was important to Nigeria's later constitutional development because it
options: removed the need for constitutional safeguards
provided a framework for sharing governmental powers between federal and regional authorities
topic_questions.explanation: The 1954 Constitution established a clearer federal distribution of powers that influenced later constitutional arrangements.

topic_questions.text: The transition from the 1960 Independence Constitution to the 1963 Republican Constitution mainly involved a change in
options: the constitutional status of the head of state
the existence of a national legislature
topic_questions.explanation: The major change was Nigeria's replacement of the British monarch with a Nigerian President as head of state.

topic_questions.text: The Nigerian Civil War, which began in 1967, had constitutional significance because it
options: occurred during a period of military government and state restructuring
topic_questions.explanation: The war occurred under military rule and was followed by significant changes in Nigeria's political and territorial structure.

topic_questions.text: The transition from parliamentary government to presidential government in Nigeria was intended partly to strengthen
options: separation between the executive and legislature
topic_questions.explanation: The presidential model established a clearer institutional separation between executive and legislative branches.

topic_questions.text: A major feature distinguishing Nigeria's Fourth Republic from the First Republic is that the Fourth Republic operates under
topic_questions.explanation: The Fourth Republic operates under the presidential system established by the 1999 Constitution.

topic_questions.text: The repeated use of military intervention in Nigerian politics affected constitutional development mainly by
options: interrupting civilian constitutional arrangements and introducing military decrees
topic_questions.explanation: Military interventions repeatedly suspended or altered civilian constitutional arrangements and substituted military decrees for ordinary legislative processes.

topic_questions.text: The constitutional history of Nigeria demonstrates that federalism has been used primarily as a mechanism for
options: managing diversity while maintaining a unified state
topic_questions.explanation: Federalism provides a framework for accommodating regional diversity while preserving national political unity.

topic_questions.text: The transition from colonial rule to self-government in Nigeria was significant because it progressively transferred political authority from
options: British colonial authorities to Nigerian institutions
topic_questions.explanation: Constitutional reforms gradually transferred political responsibility and authority from British colonial officials to Nigerian political institutions.

topic_questions.text: The most important constitutional difference between Nigeria's First and Fourth Republics is that the First Republic operated a
options: presidential system, while the Fourth Republic operates a parliamentary system
parliamentary system, while the Fourth Republic operates a presidential system
unitary system, while the Fourth Republic operates a confederal system
military system, while the Fourth Republic operates a monarchical system
topic_questions.explanation: The First Republic used a parliamentary system, whereas the Fourth Republic operates a presidential system.

topic_questions.text: The primary purpose of local government in Nigeria is to
options: replace state governments in all constitutional matters
exercise sovereign authority over local communities
bring government closer to the people and provide services at the grassroots
topic_questions.explanation: Local government is designed to promote grassroots participation and provide services close to local communities.

topic_questions.text: A major justification for creating local government areas is to
options: reduce the constitutional powers of the federal government
promote effective administration and political participation at the grassroots
make traditional rulers superior to elected councils
transfer foreign policy to local authorities
topic_questions.explanation: Local governments are intended to improve grassroots administration and encourage participation in governance.

topic_questions.text: Which situation best illustrates the principle of local government autonomy?
options: A council performs only duties personally assigned by a state commissioner
A council has no elected representatives
A council possesses legally recognized authority to make decisions within its jurisdiction
A council is controlled entirely by traditional rulers
topic_questions.explanation: Local autonomy involves legally recognized authority for local councils to manage specified local affairs.

topic_questions.text: One major problem that can undermine the effectiveness of local governments is
options: excessive financial dependence on higher levels of government
topic_questions.explanation: Heavy dependence on higher governments can limit the financial and administrative independence of local authorities.

topic_questions.text: The civil service is distinguished from elected political office holders mainly because civil servants
options: are career officials who assist in implementing government policies
topic_questions.explanation: Civil servants are career officials who provide continuity and professional assistance in policy implementation.

topic_questions.text: The principle of political neutrality in the civil service requires civil servants to
options: support the ruling party during elections
serve the government of the day professionally regardless of party affiliation
make political decisions on behalf of ministers
topic_questions.explanation: Political neutrality requires civil servants to serve the government impartially rather than operate as party activists.

topic_questions.text: A permanent secretary remains in office while ministers change after an election. This illustrates the civil service principle of
topic_questions.explanation: Career officials provide continuity in administration despite changes in political leadership.

topic_questions.text: The anonymity of civil servants traditionally means that
options: civil servants cannot be dismissed under any circumstances
official advice is normally presented publicly through the responsible political office holder
civil servants are prohibited from communicating with ministers
civil servants cannot be held accountable for misconduct
topic_questions.explanation: The traditional principle of anonymity means ministers publicly take responsibility for departmental decisions and advice.

topic_questions.text: A major advantage of the merit principle in recruitment into the civil service is that it
options: ensures appointment primarily on relevant competence and qualifications
guarantees every applicant a government position
allows political parties to select permanent officials
topic_questions.explanation: Merit-based recruitment seeks to select personnel according to competence, qualifications and suitability.

topic_questions.text: The principle of anonymity is most likely to be weakened when civil servants
options: publicly engage in partisan political disputes
topic_questions.explanation: Public partisan activity conflicts with the traditional expectation that civil servants remain politically neutral and professionally discreet.

topic_questions.text: A public corporation differs from an ordinary government ministry mainly because it is established to
options: perform specific commercial or public functions with some managerial autonomy
topic_questions.explanation: Public corporations are established for specialized public or commercial functions and generally enjoy greater operational autonomy than ministries.

topic_questions.text: Government may establish a public corporation rather than place an activity directly under a ministry when it wants
options: to transfer constitutional sovereignty to managers
greater operational flexibility in providing a specialized service
topic_questions.explanation: Public corporations can provide specialized services with more managerial flexibility while remaining publicly accountable.

topic_questions.text: One common criticism of public corporations is that they may
options: be unable to provide specialized services
suffer from political interference and weak financial accountability
topic_questions.explanation: Political interference, poor management and weak accountability can reduce the effectiveness of public corporations.

topic_questions.text: The conversion or sale of a state-owned enterprise to private ownership is most directly associated with
topic_questions.explanation: Privatization involves transferring ownership or control of a state-owned enterprise to private interests.

topic_questions.text: Commercialization of a public enterprise primarily seeks to
options: make the enterprise operate more efficiently according to commercial principles
transfer its constitutional functions to parliament
place its employees under traditional rulers
topic_questions.explanation: Commercialization aims to improve efficiency by requiring an enterprise to operate with greater attention to revenue and costs.

topic_questions.text: Traditional institutions in contemporary Nigeria generally perform an important role by
options: serving as links between communities and formal governmental institutions
topic_questions.explanation: Traditional rulers often facilitate communication, mediation and community mobilization between citizens and formal government.

topic_questions.text: The authority of traditional rulers in modern Nigeria is limited primarily because
options: they are prohibited from participating in community affairs
all traditional institutions were constitutionally abolished
their powers operate within the framework of the modern state and applicable laws
topic_questions.explanation: Traditional institutions retain cultural and community roles but operate within the legal framework of the modern state.

topic_questions.text: A traditional ruler mediates a dispute between two communities and encourages both sides to accept a settlement. This illustrates the institution's role in
topic_questions.explanation: Traditional rulers can contribute to peaceful settlement of local disputes and promote social cohesion.

topic_questions.text: A major administrative function of local governments is the maintenance of
options: certain local infrastructure and community services
topic_questions.explanation: Local governments are responsible for various grassroots services and local infrastructure within their assigned functions.

topic_questions.text: The existence of elected councillors in local government is intended primarily to
options: increase grassroots representation in local decision-making
give councils authority over international treaties
topic_questions.explanation: Elected councillors provide representation and participation in local governance.

topic_questions.text: When a local council prepares a budget for sanitation, markets and local roads, it is exercising
topic_questions.explanation: Budgeting for local services reflects the administrative and developmental responsibilities of local government.

topic_questions.text: A major reason for maintaining records and files in the civil service is to
options: preserve institutional memory and support continuity in administration
topic_questions.explanation: Official records preserve information needed for consistent administration and informed decision-making.

topic_questions.text: The doctrine of ministerial responsibility means that a minister is politically accountable for
options: the decisions and activities of the ministry under the minister's supervision
all judicial decisions in the country
the private activities of every civil servant
topic_questions.explanation: Ministers are politically responsible for the administration and policies of their departments.

topic_questions.text: A civil servant who deliberately alters an official financial record for personal benefit violates the principle of
topic_questions.explanation: Altering official records for personal gain violates integrity and ethical standards in public administration.

topic_questions.text: One reason civil service rules are standardized is to
options: make every civil servant a political appointee
prevent ministries from performing specialized functions
promote consistency, discipline and predictable administrative procedures
transfer administrative power to traditional rulers
topic_questions.explanation: Standardized rules promote consistency, discipline and orderly administration across the public service.

topic_questions.text: A public corporation that receives government funding but generates revenue from its services illustrates the combination of
topic_questions.explanation: Public corporations can remain government-owned while generating revenue through commercial activities.

topic_questions.text: Government supervision of a public corporation is justified mainly because
options: the corporation uses public resources or performs functions of public interest
public corporations are completely private organizations
the judiciary owns all public enterprises
topic_questions.explanation: Government oversight helps ensure that public resources and publicly important functions are properly managed.

topic_questions.text: A traditional council advises a state government on customary matters affecting a community. This relationship demonstrates
options: cooperation between traditional institutions and modern government
topic_questions.explanation: Traditional institutions can provide cultural knowledge and community perspectives to formal government.

topic_questions.text: Which administrative problem is most likely to result from excessive political interference in the civil service?
topic_questions.explanation: Excessive political interference can compromise neutrality and professional standards in the civil service.

topic_questions.text: A local government that depends heavily on grants from higher governments may experience difficulty because
options: it automatically becomes a private organization
its councillors lose all representative functions
local citizens cease to need public services
its ability to independently plan and execute projects may be restricted
topic_questions.explanation: Financial dependence can limit the council's ability to determine and implement its own development priorities.

topic_questions.text: The primary distinction between decentralization and deconcentration is that decentralization generally involves
options: transferring some authority to lower or semi-autonomous bodies, while deconcentration mainly redistributes functions within the central administration
giving local governments control of foreign policy
topic_questions.explanation: Decentralization transfers authority to lower bodies, while deconcentration mainly distributes central administrative functions geographically or organizationally.

topic_questions.text: If a ministry establishes regional offices that remain fully under its central control, the arrangement is best described as
topic_questions.explanation: Deconcentration involves distributing administrative responsibilities within the same central governmental structure.

topic_questions.text: A major benefit of decentralizing administrative functions is that decisions can be
options: made only by the federal cabinet
adapted more closely to local conditions and needs
topic_questions.explanation: Decentralization can make administration more responsive to local circumstances.

topic_questions.text: An effective local government requires accountability because
options: local officials should be able to spend public funds without explanation
local government has no public responsibilities
traditional rulers must approve every expenditure
public resources and decisions should be subject to appropriate scrutiny
topic_questions.explanation: Accountability ensures that local officials can be questioned about decisions and the use of public resources.

topic_questions.text: The merit system can be undermined when appointments are made primarily on the basis of
topic_questions.explanation: Appointments based mainly on political connections weaken merit-based recruitment.

topic_questions.text: A key reason for training civil servants is to
options: improve their competence and ability to perform administrative duties
make them independent of all government policies
topic_questions.explanation: Training develops the skills and knowledge required for effective public administration.

topic_questions.text: When a public corporation is required to submit audited accounts for examination, the requirement primarily promotes
topic_questions.explanation: Audited accounts allow financial activities to be examined and promote responsible management of public resources.

topic_questions.text: A government enterprise is commercialized but remains publicly owned. This means that
options: the government has completely abandoned ownership
the enterprise has become a local government
its employees have become elected officials
the enterprise is expected to operate more efficiently using commercial principles
topic_questions.explanation: Commercialization changes the operating principles of a public enterprise without necessarily transferring ownership to private interests.

topic_questions.text: The role of traditional institutions in modern Nigerian administration is strongest where they
options: mobilize communities, preserve cultural values and assist in resolving local disputes
exercise exclusive control over elected councils
appoint members of the National Assembly
topic_questions.explanation: Traditional institutions can contribute through community mobilization, cultural preservation and local mediation.

topic_questions.text: A civil servant is transferred from one ministry to another after serving under different political administrations. This demonstrates
topic_questions.explanation: Career mobility across administrations reflects the continuity and neutrality expected of professional civil servants.

topic_questions.text: A major advantage of having local representatives elected by residents is that it can
options: eliminate the need for national elections
make local officials accountable to foreign governments
topic_questions.explanation: Elected local representatives can be held accountable by residents and are therefore encouraged to respond to local priorities.

topic_questions.text: If a local government collects lawful local revenues and uses them to provide approved services, it is exercising
topic_questions.explanation: Revenue collection and expenditure on approved local services are components of local fiscal and administrative functions.

topic_questions.text: The main danger of excessive bureaucratic procedures in public administration is that they may
options: cause delays and reduce administrative efficiency
strengthen local autonomy in every case
topic_questions.explanation: Excessive procedures can create unnecessary delays, red tape and inefficiency.

topic_questions.text: The civil service differs from a public corporation because the civil service primarily
options: forms part of the permanent administrative machinery of government
has authority to amend the constitution
topic_questions.explanation: The civil service forms part of the continuing administrative machinery that supports government.

topic_questions.text: When a local government consults residents before deciding where to locate a community health facility, it is promoting
topic_questions.explanation: Consulting residents allows citizens to participate directly in decisions affecting their community.

topic_questions.text: A public corporation may be preferable to a ministry for managing a commercial service because the corporation generally
options: has no responsibility to the public
can enjoy greater managerial flexibility while pursuing a defined public purpose
topic_questions.explanation: Public corporations are often given managerial flexibility to operate specialized services more efficiently.

topic_questions.text: A traditional institution contributes most effectively to modern governance when it
options: works within the law while using its community influence to support peace and development
topic_questions.explanation: Traditional institutions can support governance effectively when their community role complements rather than replaces constitutional institutions.

topic_questions.text: The principle of hierarchy in the civil service means that
options: all civil servants have equal authority
official responsibilities and authority are arranged through recognized levels of command
junior officials automatically control senior officials
topic_questions.explanation: Hierarchy organizes authority and responsibility through established levels of command and supervision.

topic_questions.text: A major reason for maintaining confidentiality in certain civil service matters is to
options: allow civil servants to control elections
protect sensitive official information and facilitate candid administrative advice
topic_questions.explanation: Confidentiality can protect sensitive information and allow officials to provide frank professional advice.

topic_questions.text: When a public enterprise repeatedly depends on government subsidies despite poor performance, the situation may indicate
options: weak financial performance and possible management problems
topic_questions.explanation: Persistent dependence on subsidies despite poor performance may signal inefficiency or weak management.

topic_questions.text: The effectiveness of local government is most likely to improve when there is a combination of
options: adequate resources, competent personnel, accountability and citizen participation
topic_questions.explanation: Effective local administration requires resources, capable officials, accountability and meaningful community participation.

topic_questions.text: One major reason advanced for military intervention in Nigerian politics in 1966 was
options: the complete success of civilian institutions
the desire to strengthen parliamentary government
political instability, corruption and disputed electoral processes
topic_questions.explanation: Political instability, corruption and disputed elections were among the factors cited by the military as reasons for intervention.

topic_questions.text: A fundamental feature that distinguishes military government from constitutional civilian government is that military rulers generally
options: derive their authority directly from periodic elections
assume political authority through military intervention rather than constitutional elections
are subject to routine parliamentary confidence votes
topic_questions.explanation: Military governments normally come to power through intervention rather than through constitutional electoral procedures.

topic_questions.text: The January 1966 coup was significant in Nigerian political development because it
options: ended the First Republic and introduced military rule
topic_questions.explanation: The January 1966 coup ended the First Republic and began Nigeria's first period of military rule.

topic_questions.text: A military government is usually headed by a military officer who exercises executive authority through
topic_questions.explanation: Military regimes commonly govern through decrees, proclamations and military directives rather than ordinary parliamentary legislation.

topic_questions.text: The Supreme Military Council established under the Gowon regime primarily served as
options: a judicial body for constitutional disputes
a central decision-making organ of the military government
topic_questions.explanation: The Supreme Military Council was a major policy and decision-making institution under the Gowon military administration.

topic_questions.text: One major political consequence of military rule in Nigeria was the
options: creation of additional states to address administrative and political concerns
topic_questions.explanation: Successive military governments created additional states partly to improve administration and respond to political demands.

topic_questions.text: The 1967 creation of twelve states was especially significant because it
options: replaced the former four-region structure with a new state structure
topic_questions.explanation: The 1967 state creation exercise replaced the previous regional arrangement with twelve states.

topic_questions.text: The Unification Decree No. 34 of 1966 was intended primarily to
options: establish a more centralized form of government
increase the powers of political parties
topic_questions.explanation: Decree No. 34 sought to replace the federal arrangement with a more centralized unitary structure.

topic_questions.text: One reason the Gowon administration reversed the unification policy was the
options: demand for a return to colonial rule
need to respond to strong opposition to excessive centralization
topic_questions.explanation: Strong opposition to excessive centralization contributed to the abandonment of the unitary direction associated with Decree No. 34.

topic_questions.text: The creation of states during military rule was partly intended to
options: reduce the dominance of larger political units and improve administration
topic_questions.explanation: State creation was often presented as a means of improving representation, administration and minority inclusion.

topic_questions.text: The Gowon regime is particularly associated with the policy of
options: reconstruction, rehabilitation and reconciliation after the civil war
immediate privatization of all public enterprises
topic_questions.explanation: After the civil war, the Gowon administration emphasized reconstruction, rehabilitation and reconciliation.

topic_questions.text: A major source of increased government revenue during the Gowon era was
options: the growing importance of petroleum exports
topic_questions.explanation: Petroleum became increasingly important to government revenue during the Gowon period.

topic_questions.text: The military administration of Murtala Mohammed is remembered for
options: introducing a more determined programme of political reforms and transition to civilian rule
topic_questions.explanation: The Murtala administration pursued significant political reforms and began a transition programme toward civilian government.

topic_questions.text: The 1976 local government reforms were important because they sought to
options: place all local administration under traditional rulers
remove elected participation from local government
establish a more uniform and viable local government system
topic_questions.explanation: The 1976 reforms aimed to standardize local government structure and strengthen it as a recognized tier of administration.

topic_questions.text: The transition programme under the Murtala and Obasanjo administration eventually culminated in
options: the transfer of power to an elected civilian government in 1979
the restoration of the First Republic
the abolition of the federal system
topic_questions.explanation: The military transition programme led to the return of civilian government under the 1979 Constitution.

topic_questions.text: The Second Republic differed from the First Republic mainly because it operated a
topic_questions.explanation: The Second Republic was based on the 1979 presidential constitution rather than the parliamentary system of the First Republic.

topic_questions.text: The 1983 military coup that ended the Second Republic was partly justified by its leaders on the grounds of
options: corruption, electoral malpractice and economic difficulties
topic_questions.explanation: The military cited corruption, electoral problems and economic difficulties among the reasons for intervention.

topic_questions.text: The Buhari-Idiagbon regime differed from earlier civilian administrations mainly in its emphasis on
options: discipline, accountability and strict administrative control
topic_questions.explanation: The Buhari-Idiagbon administration emphasized discipline, accountability and strict control of public conduct.

topic_questions.text: A major criticism of the Buhari-Idiagbon administration was that
options: its methods of enforcing discipline were considered authoritarian
topic_questions.explanation: The regime's strict measures and restrictions on political freedoms attracted criticism for authoritarianism.

topic_questions.text: The Babangida administration came to power in 1985 after
options: the collapse of the Fourth Republic
the removal of the Buhari-Idiagbon government
the election of a new civilian president
the restoration of the First Republic
topic_questions.explanation: Ibrahim Babangida became military head of state after the August 1985 coup that removed Buhari from office.

topic_questions.text: A distinctive feature of the Babangida transition programme was the
options: permanent suspension of all political activity
creation and sponsorship of two government-approved political parties
topic_questions.explanation: The Babangida administration created the SDP and NRC as the two officially recognized parties during its transition programme.

topic_questions.text: The annulment of the 12 June 1993 presidential election significantly affected the transition programme by
options: bringing the transition to a successful conclusion
creating a major political crisis and disrupting the transition
topic_questions.explanation: The annulment created a serious legitimacy crisis and disrupted the planned transition to civilian rule.

topic_questions.text: The Interim National Government of 1993 was established mainly as
options: a temporary political arrangement following the annulment crisis
a return to the First Republic
topic_questions.explanation: The ING was established as an interim arrangement during the political crisis following the annulment of the 12 June election.

topic_questions.text: The Abacha regime is associated with the suspension or restriction of
topic_questions.explanation: The Abacha regime maintained tight political control and restricted democratic political activity.

topic_questions.text: The transition programme under General Abdulsalami Abubakar was significant because it
options: provided a relatively rapid route toward the Fourth Republic
topic_questions.explanation: The Abdulsalami administration implemented a transition programme that culminated in the 1999 return to civilian rule.

topic_questions.text: A major condition necessary for successful military disengagement from politics is
options: credible civilian institutions capable of maintaining political stability
topic_questions.explanation: Stable and credible civilian institutions are necessary to sustain democratic governance after military withdrawal.

topic_questions.text: One argument commonly used to justify military intervention is that the military can
options: restore order when civilian political institutions are perceived to have become ineffective
topic_questions.explanation: Military leaders have often justified intervention by claiming that civilian institutions have failed to maintain order or good governance.

topic_questions.text: A major weakness of military rule in relation to constitutional government is that
options: military governments always have too many elected representatives
political authority is not normally derived from competitive constitutional elections
military regimes cannot create administrative institutions
topic_questions.explanation: Military governments generally assume power outside normal constitutional electoral processes.

topic_questions.text: The creation of states can contribute to political stability when it
options: provides smaller groups with greater access to governmental institutions
topic_questions.explanation: Smaller administrative units can provide minority groups with greater political representation and access to government.

topic_questions.text: The military's suspension of elected legislatures during military rule illustrates the replacement of
options: constitutional civilian institutions with military structures
topic_questions.explanation: Military regimes commonly suspend elected institutions and replace them with appointed military governing bodies.

topic_questions.text: A major difference between military and civilian political parties is that under military rule
options: political parties are commonly suspended or restricted
parties normally control the military government
topic_questions.explanation: Military governments commonly suspend political parties and restrict partisan political activity.

topic_questions.text: The transition from military to civilian rule is most complete when
options: military officers retain final political authority
elected civilian institutions regain constitutional control over government
military decrees permanently replace the constitution
topic_questions.explanation: A genuine transition requires elected civilian institutions to exercise constitutional authority over government.

topic_questions.text: The National Youth Service Corps scheme, introduced during military rule, was intended partly to
options: promote national integration among Nigerian youths
topic_questions.explanation: The NYSC scheme was designed to promote national integration and interaction among young Nigerians.

topic_questions.text: A major reason for establishing the NYSC after the civil war was the need to
options: transfer local government powers to the military
promote national unity and understanding among young Nigerians
topic_questions.explanation: The scheme was introduced partly to encourage national integration following the divisions associated with the civil war.

topic_questions.text: The Structural Adjustment Programme introduced under the Babangida administration sought primarily to
options: restructure the economy and reduce excessive dependence on government controls
topic_questions.explanation: SAP aimed to restructure the Nigerian economy through measures including deregulation, reduced controls and greater reliance on market forces.

topic_questions.text: One major criticism of the Structural Adjustment Programme was that it
options: imposed social costs and economic hardship on some groups
topic_questions.explanation: SAP policies were criticized for their social and economic effects, including hardship associated with adjustment measures.

topic_questions.text: The transition programme of a military regime becomes less credible when
options: political parties are allowed to organize
elections are prepared under constitutional rules
the military repeatedly changes transition dates or political rules
topic_questions.explanation: Repeated changes to transition schedules or political rules can reduce confidence in the sincerity of military disengagement.

topic_questions.text: The 1999 return to civilian rule is generally regarded as significant because it
options: marked the beginning of the Fourth Republic
topic_questions.explanation: The transfer of power to an elected civilian government in 1999 marked the beginning of the Fourth Republic.

topic_questions.text: A military regime may claim to fight corruption, but its legitimacy is weakened if
options: it fails to operate under accountable and transparent political institutions
topic_questions.explanation: Anti-corruption policies do not by themselves establish democratic legitimacy; accountability and lawful institutions remain important.

topic_questions.text: The frequent intervention of the military in Nigerian politics historically contributed to

topic_questions.explanation: Repeated military interventions interrupted civilian constitutional arrangements and delayed sustained democratic development.

topic_questions.explanation: Prolonged military intervention can weaken democratic habits and the development of stable civilian political institutions.

topic_questions.text: A major institutional requirement for preventing future military intervention is the development of
options: strong democratic institutions and constitutional civilian oversight
political parties controlled by the armed forces
topic_questions.explanation: Strong democratic institutions, constitutionalism and civilian oversight can help reduce the conditions that encourage military intervention.

topic_questions.text: The political significance of the Second Republic lies partly in its demonstration that Nigeria

could transfer from military rule to an elected presidential government
topic_questions.explanation: The Second Republic demonstrated a return from military government to elected presidential civilian government.

topic_questions.text: The political significance of the 1983 coup was that it
options: interrupted the Second Republic and returned Nigeria to military rule
topic_questions.explanation: The December 1983 coup ended the Second Republic and began another period of military government.

topic_questions.text: The overall pattern of military intervention in Nigeria suggests that military rule was often followed by
options: attempts to design new constitutional arrangements and transition programmes
the permanent abolition of civilian institutions
the immediate restoration of colonial rule
the elimination of federalism from every constitution
topic_questions.explanation: Military regimes repeatedly introduced transition programmes and constitutional reforms intended to return the country to civilian rule.

topic_questions.text: A military transition programme is most likely to succeed when it
options: sets credible procedures for elections and transfers power to legitimate civilian institutions
keeps the military as the final political authority
topic_questions.explanation: Successful disengagement requires credible elections, functioning civilian institutions and an actual transfer of political authority.

topic_questions.text: A major lesson from Nigeria's repeated military interventions is that democratic stability requires
options: constitutional institutions capable of resolving political conflicts peacefully
permanent military supervision of civilian governments
government by decree during political crises
topic_questions.explanation: Strong constitutional institutions can provide peaceful mechanisms for resolving political disputes and reducing the appeal of military intervention.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's foreign policy is best understood as the set of principles guiding its relations with
options: other states and actors in the international system
topic_questions.explanation: Foreign policy covers a state's principles and actions in dealing with other states and relevant international actors.

topic_questions.text: The principle of non-alignment in Nigeria's foreign policy originally implied that Nigeria would
options: avoid diplomatic relations with major powers
avoid formal alignment with competing Cold War power blocs
withdraw from all international economic activities
topic_questions.explanation: Non-alignment meant avoiding formal attachment to either major Cold War bloc while maintaining independent relations.

topic_questions.text: A major objective of Nigeria's foreign policy since independence has been the promotion of
options: African unity and the elimination of colonialism
economic isolation from other African states
topic_questions.explanation: Nigeria has consistently emphasized African unity, decolonization and opposition to colonial and racial domination.

topic_questions.text: The principle that Nigeria's foreign policy should be guided primarily by its national interests means that
options: Nigeria must avoid all international commitments
foreign relations should support the country's security, prosperity and strategic objectives
Nigeria should always support the strongest global power
African issues should never influence foreign policy
topic_questions.explanation: National interest requires foreign-policy decisions to advance important national goals such as security and economic development.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's emphasis on African unity is closely associated with the belief that
options: African states should surrender their sovereignty
only military alliances can solve African problems
African countries share interests that can be advanced through collective action
foreign powers should determine African policies
topic_questions.explanation: Nigeria has promoted collective African action because of shared political, economic and security interests.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's active role in the formation and development of the Organization of African Unity was mainly intended to promote
topic_questions.explanation: The OAU was established to promote African unity, cooperation and the struggle against colonialism and apartheid.

topic_questions.text: The transformation of the OAU into the African Union reflected a desire to create
options: a stronger framework for African integration and collective action
a replacement for all national governments
an organization controlled exclusively by Nigeria
topic_questions.explanation: The African Union was designed to strengthen continental integration, cooperation and collective responses to African challenges.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's participation in peacekeeping operations is an example of its commitment to
options: regional and international peace and security
ending the authority of the United Nations
topic_questions.explanation: Nigeria has contributed personnel and resources to peacekeeping as part of its international security role.

topic_questions.text: The Economic Community of West African States was established primarily to promote
options: economic integration and cooperation among member states
the abolition of national borders worldwide
topic_questions.explanation: ECOWAS was created to promote economic integration and cooperation among West African states.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's leading role in ECOWAS is particularly important because
options: Nigeria has historically possessed substantial economic, demographic and diplomatic influence in West Africa
Nigeria controls every West African government
ECOWAS membership is restricted to Nigeria
Nigeria has no economic interests in the region
topic_questions.explanation: Nigeria's population, economy and regional influence have contributed to its prominent role within ECOWAS.

topic_questions.text: The ECOWAS Monitoring Group became particularly prominent in conflicts involving
options: West African countries such as Liberia and Sierra Leone
topic_questions.explanation: ECOMOG was deployed prominently in conflicts in Liberia and Sierra Leone to support regional peace and security.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's membership of the United Nations enables it to
options: exercise permanent veto power in the Security Council
participate in global discussions and collective international action
control the policies of all member states
avoid obligations arising from international agreements
topic_questions.explanation: UN membership gives Nigeria a platform for diplomacy, negotiations and participation in collective international activities.

topic_questions.text: The United Nations Security Council differs from the General Assembly because the Security Council has primary responsibility for
options: managing the economies of member states
topic_questions.explanation: The Security Council has primary responsibility within the UN system for maintaining international peace and security.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's campaign for greater representation of developing countries in the UN Security Council is based largely on the argument that
options: developing countries should control the entire UN
Africa should withdraw from the UN
the existing structure does not adequately reflect contemporary global realities
permanent membership should be abolished immediately
topic_questions.explanation: Nigeria supports Security Council reform because the present composition is widely viewed as insufficiently representative of today's international system.

topic_questions.text: The Commonwealth has been important to Nigeria's foreign relations mainly because of
options: shared historical, institutional and diplomatic connections among member states
Nigeria's obligation to obey British domestic laws
topic_questions.explanation: Historical links and common institutional and diplomatic relationships have made Commonwealth membership relevant to Nigeria.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's foreign policy toward apartheid South Africa was characterized principally by
options: opposition to apartheid and support for liberation movements
topic_questions.explanation: Nigeria strongly opposed apartheid and supported the struggle for majority rule in Southern Africa.

topic_questions.text: The policy of using Nigeria's economic resources to support African liberation movements illustrates the idea of
options: Africa as the centrepiece of Nigerian foreign policy
topic_questions.explanation: Supporting African liberation movements reflected Nigeria's commitment to African interests as a central foreign-policy priority.

topic_questions.text: A country may establish diplomatic relations with another state primarily to
options: transfer its constitution to the other state
topic_questions.explanation: Diplomatic relations provide channels for communication, negotiation and cooperation between states.

topic_questions.text: The appointment of an ambassador is significant because an ambassador primarily
options: commands the host country's armed forces
makes laws for the host country
represents the sending state in the host country
topic_questions.explanation: An ambassador is the official diplomatic representative of one state in another state.

topic_questions.text: Consular services are especially concerned with
options: assisting citizens abroad and handling certain administrative matters
topic_questions.explanation: Consular offices commonly assist nationals abroad and provide services such as documentation and related administrative support.

topic_questions.text: Foreign aid becomes an instrument of foreign policy when a state uses assistance to
options: advance diplomatic, economic or strategic objectives
topic_questions.explanation: Aid can serve foreign-policy purposes by strengthening relationships and advancing economic or strategic interests.

topic_questions.text: Economic diplomacy is primarily concerned with using international relations to promote
topic_questions.explanation: Economic diplomacy seeks to advance trade, investment and other economic interests through external relations.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's membership of international organizations can promote its national interest by
options: preventing it from negotiating with other states
providing platforms for negotiation, cooperation and influence
requiring it to accept every foreign policy of larger states
topic_questions.explanation: International organizations give Nigeria opportunities to negotiate, cooperate and influence collective decisions.

topic_questions.text: The principle of peaceful settlement of disputes requires states to
options: use force as their first option
submit every domestic issue to foreign governments
seek negotiation, mediation, arbitration or other peaceful means
topic_questions.explanation: Peaceful settlement involves resolving disputes through non-violent mechanisms such as negotiation, mediation and arbitration.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's participation in international mediation is consistent with its desire to
options: promote peace and stability beyond its immediate borders
control the governments of neighbouring states
topic_questions.explanation: Mediation allows Nigeria to contribute diplomatically to resolving conflicts and promoting regional stability.

topic_questions.text: A major advantage of regional integration for Nigeria is that it can
options: expand markets and facilitate regional economic cooperation
end diplomatic relations with non-African countries
topic_questions.explanation: Regional integration can increase market access, trade and economic cooperation among participating states.

topic_questions.text: The principle of territorial integrity means that states should respect
options: only the economic policies of powerful countries
the right of foreign governments to redraw borders
the territorial boundaries and political independence of other states
topic_questions.explanation: Territorial integrity requires respect for states' established territories and political independence.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's foreign policy can be affected by domestic economic conditions because
options: foreign policy is completely independent of national resources
economic weakness may reduce the resources available for diplomatic initiatives
international relations never involve economic interests
domestic politics has no connection with external policy
topic_questions.explanation: A state's economic capacity affects its ability to finance diplomacy, peacekeeping and other foreign-policy initiatives.

topic_questions.text: One reason Nigeria places strong emphasis on relations with neighbouring states is that
options: neighbours have no effect on national security
border issues, migration, trade and security directly affect Nigeria
Nigeria is constitutionally prohibited from dealing with distant states
neighbouring countries control Nigeria's foreign ministry
topic_questions.explanation: Relations with neighbouring countries directly affect Nigeria's security, trade, migration and border management.

topic_questions.text: The principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of states is intended primarily to
options: discourage states from unlawfully interfering in the domestic affairs of other sovereign states
prevent all forms of international cooperation
topic_questions.explanation: Non-interference protects state sovereignty by discouraging unlawful external intervention in domestic affairs.

topic_questions.text: The African Union's principle of collective security means that member states
options: can cooperate in responding to threats to peace and security
cannot criticize unconstitutional changes of government
topic_questions.explanation: Collective security involves cooperation among states to address threats to peace and stability.

topic_questions.text: The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea is particularly relevant to Nigeria because of its
options: position as a coastal state with maritime interests
topic_questions.explanation: As a coastal state, Nigeria has significant interests in maritime boundaries, navigation and offshore resources.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's foreign policy toward its citizens living abroad may include efforts to
options: protect their legitimate interests through diplomatic and consular channels
topic_questions.explanation: Diplomatic and consular missions can assist and protect Nigerian citizens abroad within the limits of international law.

topic_questions.text: The concept of national interest prevents a state from treating foreign policy as
options: a means of promoting national security
an activity unrelated to national priorities
topic_questions.explanation: Foreign policy is expected to serve national priorities rather than operate independently of national interests.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's role in the Non-Aligned Movement historically reflected its preference for
options: exclusive alignment with the Soviet Union
exclusive alignment with the United States
topic_questions.explanation: Non-alignment emphasized independent decision-making rather than formal attachment to either Cold War bloc.

topic_questions.text: A foreign-policy decision based on the protection of Nigeria's oil supply routes would primarily reflect
topic_questions.explanation: Protecting vital energy routes relates directly to national security and economic interests.

topic_questions.text: International treaties become especially important to foreign policy because they
options: create agreed obligations and frameworks for cooperation between states
apply only to domestic political parties
topic_questions.explanation: Treaties establish agreed rules, commitments and mechanisms for cooperation among states.

topic_questions.text: The principle of reciprocity in diplomacy means that
options: a state must surrender its foreign policy
states may respond to another state's diplomatic treatment with comparable measures
only powerful states can exchange diplomatic privileges
topic_questions.explanation: Reciprocity involves responding to another state's treatment with corresponding diplomatic measures.

topic_questions.explanation: Nigeria supported the right of African peoples to achieve independence and self-government.

topic_questions.text: The diplomatic principle of recognition involves a state acknowledging
options: the existence or legal status of another state or government for international purposes
the superiority of another country's constitution
the abolition of its own government
the compulsory adoption of another state's currency
topic_questions.explanation: Recognition is a diplomatic act through which a state acknowledges another state's or government's status for international relations.

topic_questions.text: One major function of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is to
options: conduct Nigeria's external relations under the direction of the government
topic_questions.explanation: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is a central institution for formulating and implementing Nigeria's external relations.

topic_questions.explanation: Reducing trade barriers among states is a central feature of economic integration.

topic_questions.text: A major limitation on Nigeria's ability to pursue an ambitious foreign policy is
options: the complete absence of international institutions
limited resources and competing domestic priorities
the prohibition of diplomacy under international law
the lack of any neighbouring states
topic_questions.explanation: Foreign-policy ambitions can be constrained by financial resources, domestic needs and competing national priorities.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's leadership in African peace initiatives can increase its international influence because it
options: demonstrates willingness and capacity to contribute to regional stability
eliminates the sovereignty of other African states
prevents other states from joining organizations
topic_questions.explanation: Constructive participation in peace efforts can enhance a state's diplomatic credibility and influence.

topic_questions.text: The African Continental Free Trade Area is most closely associated with the objective of
options: increasing intra-African trade and economic integration
creating a single African military government
topic_questions.explanation: AfCFTA aims to expand trade among African countries and deepen continental economic integration.

topic_questions.explanation: Negotiation is one of the recognized peaceful methods for resolving international disputes.

topic_questions.text: The success of Nigeria's foreign policy is most meaningfully assessed by examining whether it
options: serves national interests while contributing to wider international objectives
depends entirely on the policies of powerful countries
topic_questions.explanation: Effective foreign policy should protect national interests while enabling constructive participation in international affairs.

topic_questions.explanation: Non-alignment allows a state to maintain relations with competing powers without formally joining their opposing blocs.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria's involvement in international organizations is partly intended to ensure that
options: its views and interests are represented in global decision-making
international law ceases to apply to Nigeria
topic_questions.explanation: Participation gives Nigeria opportunities to express its interests and influence collective international decisions.

topic_questions.text: The principle of sovereign equality in international relations means that
options: all states are identical in military strength
each sovereign state has equal legal status regardless of its size or power
small states must obey large states
topic_questions.explanation: Sovereign equality means states have equal legal standing in international law despite differences in size or power.

topic_questions.text: A major reason Nigeria has historically supported multilateral diplomacy is that it
options: provides opportunities for collective action and greater diplomatic influence
requires all countries to share one government
topic_questions.explanation: Multilateral diplomacy enables states to pursue shared interests and exert influence through collective institutions.
